costNodePlain: Money set aside for loans that may not be repaid — the provision for credit losses: $2.2B was charged off in the quarter and the bank added a net $598M to reserves (a $546M net build in Consumer, driven by loan growth in Card Services, and a $41M net build in Wholesale), leaving a provision of $2,762M.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost, up 18% on wage inflation, growth in front-office and technology staff, and staff added with First Republic.

opex.name: Professional & outside services
opex.note: Professional fees and outside services combined, as reported in the supplement — down 2%.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, communications and equipment — up 7% as the bank keeps investing in its platforms.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,208M of occupancy) plus other expense ($5,118M) — other expense nearly tripled, driven by the $2.9B FDIC special assessment in Corporate.

footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $39.9B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $38.6B — the $1,369M difference is a fully taxable-equivalent gross-up of tax-exempt income ($126M in net interest income and $1,243M in noninterest revenue) that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue, and operating profit here is income before income taxes.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago

kpis.label: Credit costs
kpis.note: $2.2B of net charge-offs and a $598M net reserve build

oneTimers: $2.9B FDIC special assessment in Corporate — the release's flagged 'significant item' for 4Q23, the bank's share of refilling the Deposit Insurance Fund after the 2023 bank failures. It reduced EPS by $0.74; excluding significant items, net income was $12.1B ($3.97 per share) instead of $9.3B ($3.04). It sits inside other expense, in the 'Occupancy & other expense' bucket on this page.

$743M of net investment securities losses in Corporate, primarily from sales of U.S. Treasuries and mortgage-backed securities (versus $874M of net securities losses in 4Q22, largely offset then by a $914M gain on the sale of Visa B shares).

First Republic (acquired May 1, 2023) contributed $647M of net income in the quarter — $1.3B of net interest income and $533M of noninterest revenue, less $890M of noninterest expense and a $125M provision for credit losses.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 19% on higher rates and the First Republic portfolio, partly offset by lower deposit balances.

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — up just 1% on a reported basis, as higher asset management and Investment Banking fees were partly offset by $743M of net investment securities losses in Corporate; the year-ago quarter included a $914M gain on the sale of Visa B shares.

takeaways.text: Reported net interest income rose 19% to $24.1B — 62% of all revenue — on higher rates, higher revolving card balances and the First Republic loan book, even as deposit balances fell.
takeaways.title: Interest income surged

takeaways.text: The $2.9B FDIC special assessment (in Corporate, inside other expense) cut EPS by $0.74. Excluding it and $743M of net investment securities losses, net income was $12.1B, or $3.97 per share; full-year 2023 net income was a record $49.6B.
takeaways.title: The FDIC charge hid a record year

takeaways.text: The provision rose 21% YoY to $2,762M: $2.2B of net charge-offs — mostly normalizing Card Services losses — plus a $598M net reserve build, versus a $1.4B reserve build a year ago.
takeaways.title: Credit costs normalized upward

verdict: JPMorgan's reported revenue rose 12% to $38.6B, but a $2.9B FDIC special assessment pulled net income down 15% to $9.3B — excluding the quarter's significant items, profit was $12.1B.
